summary: Defines MIB objects, in SMIv2 format, for managing ATM interfaces, devices, networks and services with SNMP. This is version 8.0 of the ATM management definitions. It has been replaced by RFC 2515.

eli5.summary: A set of named gauges that let a network manager check on equipment using a type of fast cell-based network called ATM.

subtitle: SNMP management objects for ATM networks and devices.

tldr.problem: ATM networks and interfaces need to be monitored and managed, but there was no standard way to do this using SNMP, the universal network management protocol.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1695 defines a complete MIB with objects to manage ATM interfaces, virtual connections, traffic parameters, and performance statistics.
tldr.outcome: This specification enabled SNMP-based management of ATM networks and was later enhanced by RFC 2515, which added support for additional ATM features and refinements.

today: RFC 1695 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 2515, which provides updated and expanded ATM MIB definitions. The newer RFC adds support for additional ATM features and provides clarifications based on implementation experience.

sections.title: Introduction to ATM Management
sections.content:
RFC 1695 defines a Management Information Base (MIB) for managing Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) interfaces, devices, networks and services using SNMP. This version 8.0 extends the SNMPv2 framework to cover the specific needs of ATM deployments.

ATM is a high-speed cell-switched technology that operates at the data link layer. Unlike traditional packet-switched networks, ATM divides data into fixed 53-byte cells and switches them at very high speeds. The MIB must track both physical interfaces and virtual connections across these cells.
sections.eli5: ATM is a super-fast way to send data in tiny fixed-size chunks called cells. This RFC explains how to check on ATM equipment using SNMP, like checking the health of any other network device.

sections.title: ATM Virtual Connections
sections.content:
ATM uses two types of virtual connections: Virtual Channel Connections (VCCs) and Virtual Path Connections (VPCs). A VCC is a connection between two endpoints for user data; a VPC is a bundle of VCCs that share the same path through the network.

Virtual connections span multiple devices and switches, with each hop represented as a virtual link (VCL for channels, VPL for paths). A Permanent Virtual Connection (PVC) is manually provisioned and stays active. A Switched Virtual Connection (SVC) is set up on demand via signaling. Each connection can be point-to-point, point-to-multipoint, or multipoint-to-multipoint.
sections.eli5: Think of VCCs and VPCs as pipelines: a VCC is one dedicated pipe between two places, and a VPC is a highway that carries multiple VCCs together. Some pipes are permanent (PVC), and some are set up when needed (SVC).

sections.title: Traffic Management and Quality of Service
sections.content:
The MIB tracks several traffic management mechanisms. Usage Parameter Control (UPC) polices incoming traffic to ensure it does not exceed negotiated rates; traffic shaping smooths outgoing traffic. The MIB monitors traffic descriptor parameters like peak cell rate.

ATM assigns each cell one of two Cell Loss Priority (CLP) values. Cells marked CLP=0 get preferential treatment during congestion. The MIB also tracks Quality of Service (QoS) classes (0 through 4) which define acceptable cell loss, delay, and delay variation for different service types: constant bit rate, variable bit rate, connection-oriented data, and connectionless data.
sections.eli5: ATM networks control traffic like a highway: some lanes are marked as high-priority to avoid traffic jams, and different types of traffic (video, data, etc.) get different treatment based on how sensitive they are to delays or drops.

sections.title: MIB Organization
sections.content:
The ATM MIB is organized into six main groups. The ATM Interface Configuration Group manages local ATM interface setup. The DS3 PLCP and TC Layer Groups provide performance statistics for the physical transmission layers carrying ATM cells.

The ATM Virtual Link Configuration Groups manage creation and modification of VCCs and VPCs in hosts, switches, and networks. The Cross-Connect Groups manage interconnections between virtual links in switches and networks. The AAL5 Performance Statistics Group tracks the ATM Adaptation Layer 5, which bridges user applications to the cell layer.
sections.eli5: The MIB is organized like a toolbox with separate compartments: one for interfaces, one for virtual pipes, one for switching, one for quality checks, and so on.

sections.title: Integration with SNMP and MIB II
sections.content:
The ATM MIB integrates with the standard MIB II for general system and interface management. ATM interfaces are represented as entries in the standard ifTable, with the ifType value 37 designated for ATM. The ifSpeed object reports the total bandwidth in bits per second for the ATM layer.

The RFC notes that complete ATM network management requires additional MIB modules for physical layer management (DS3, SONET), application-specific management (SMDS), and other protocol-specific needs. The ATM MIB itself focuses on the ATM cell layer and virtual connection management.
sections.eli5: The ATM objects fit into the standard SNMP toolbox so they work alongside gauges for other network equipment and protocols.

sections.title: Permanent and Switched Connections
sections.content:
The MIB is primarily designed to manage Permanent Virtual Connections (PVCs), which are provisioned manually and remain stable. PVCs are ideal for point-to-point links and dedicated services like Frame Relay over ATM.

The MIB also supports Switched Virtual Connections (SVCs), which are set up and torn down on demand through signaling procedures. However, the RFC acknowledges that full SVC management may require additional capabilities beyond the scope of this specification, such as call setup and teardown automation.
sections.eli5: The MIB handles permanent pipes well, and it can track temporary pipes too, though managing temporary pipes fully would need extra features.
